newsitem.title: USA: Miami says may scrap $25 million TANs sale.
newsitem.headline: Miami says may scrap $25 million TANs sale.

text.p: The City of Miami probably will cancel plans to issue $25 million of tax anticipation notes and instead seek short-term loans from local banks to meet cash flow needs, Assistant City Manager Bill Hampton told Reuters Monday.
The city declared a fiscal crisis Monday, citing a $68 million budget deficit for fiscal 1997, which began Oct 1.
The worsening financial situation would probably preclude any note sale at this time, Hampton said.
"We might be able to get TANs but the interest rates would be very high," Hampton said. "At this stage of the game it looks like it would not be possible."

The city has issued tax anticipation notes every year since 1989, to meet cash flow needs until property tax receipts start coming in. It planned to issue $25 million of TANs in October or early November but a resolution authorizing the issue was postponed while the city struggled to sort out its budget.

The TAN proposal had already been sent to rating agencies. Standard & Poor's Corp placed its single-A rating for Miami's general obligation debt on CreditWatch with negative implications on Friday citing the city's deficit. Moody's Investors Service put its single-A rating under review for the same reason a week earlier.
Hampton said the city was still trying to determine how big of a short-term loan is would seek from local banks but that $25 million was probably "in the ballpark."
